Portfolio.Headline: Software Developer · Backend & AI Development
Portfolio.Bio: I graduated from UMSL in May 2026 with a B.S. in Computer Science and a minor in Psychology. Most recently I was an AI Developer Intern at BlueScope Buildings North America, turning an Azure-based RAG tool into a reusable application for answering questions about codebases and building AI workflow automation for Butler Manufacturing. In October 2026 my team won 1st place in the Hybrid Teams division at Hack Midwest 2026. I like building across the stack: backend APIs in C#, Java, and TypeScript, systems programming in C and C++, web apps in React, and games in Unity. Below are projects from my coursework and my own time.

Education.Details: Completed six cross-campus courses covering AI/ML and LLM fundamentals, unsupervised learning, cloud AI application development, NLP, and deep learning.

Resume.Summary: Computer Science graduate and 1st-place Hack Midwest 2026 winner with AI development internship experience building RAG tools and AI workflow automation. Builds backend APIs in C#, Java, and TypeScript, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines on Azure and AWS, and C/C++ systems programs on Linux. Experienced with authentication, relational databases, external API integration, and cloud deployment.

PdfUrl.Title: Software Engineering Intern
Highlights: What you built or improved, and the result.

Projects.Name: BlueScope: Codebase Q&A Tool
Highlights: Refactored an existing Azure-based RAG tool into a standalone application for ingesting and indexing different codebases, replacing repository-specific logic with reusable configuration.
Used Cursor to restructure hardcoded pipeline components while retaining Azure-generated embeddings and Azure AI Search retrieval for codebase question answering.
Validated the generalized application across several codebases, manually checking answers for correctness and grounding in the underlying source code.

Projects.Name: Butler Manufacturing: AI Workflow Automation
Projects.Tech: Copilot Studio, Microsoft Copilot, Power Automate
Highlights: Scheduled and led workflow review meetings with construction consultants, project managers, and project assistants to map their day-to-day processes and find work suited to AI automation.
Designed and built an AI agent for construction consultants that transcribes dictated speech and handwritten site notes into formatted site reports.
Planned future AI agents for the project manager and project assistant teams, laying out each workflow and the proposed solution for later development.

CS-4760-Assignment-6-Memory-Management-w.Title: Memory Management Simulator
CS-4760-Assignment-6-Memory-Management-w.Description: A memory manager with a 256-entry frame table, 32-page process tables, LRU replacement, dirty-bit tracking, and simulated disk-I/O timing, using fork/exec, System V shared memory, and message queues.

P2-Parser-and-Parse-Tree-Builder.Description: A lexical scanner and recursive-descent parser for a custom language, with tokenization, parse-tree construction, and syntax-error reporting in modular components.

bbna-hackmw26.Title: Closure Call
bbna-hackmw26.Description: AI weather-closure decision support, built by a 5-person team at Hack Midwest 2026. I was the top code contributor: ASP.NET Core endpoints for live National Weather Service observations, active alerts, per-workday commute forecasts, and NOAA storm outlooks; a "similar past days" RAG feature that ranks 332 historical Kansas City weather days against the forecast using Amazon Titan embeddings stored in SQLite, exposed as a tool for the Bedrock agent team; and the SQLite audit database behind the SHA-256 hash-chained decision log.
bbna-hackmw26.Award: 1st Place, Hybrid Teams — Hack Midwest 2026 (Kansas City, MO · October 2026)

CMP-SCI-4760-Project-4-MultiLevel-Feedba.Title: Multi-Level Feedback Queue Scheduler
CMP-SCI-4760-Project-4-MultiLevel-Feedba.Description: A three-level feedback queue CPU scheduler for up to 18 concurrent worker processes, with doubling time slices, demotion on full-slice use, and IPC cleanup on SIGINT.

Project-5-OS-Resource-Management.Title: Deadlock Detection Simulator
Project-5-OS-Resource-Management.Description: Simulates resource allocation across 5 resource types with shared memory and message queues, running deadlock detection every simulated second and recovering by terminating one deadlocked process per detection round.

Curtis-Been-CS4280-Project-P4-Target-Gen.Title: Compiler for a Custom Language
Curtis-Been-CS4280-Project-P4-Target-Gen.Description: A four-stage compiler: lexical scanner, recursive-descent parser that builds a parse tree, static semantics checking, and assembly code generation with storage allocation. A global symbol table enforces semantic rules, stopping on errors such as use-before-definition and redefinition while reporting warnings without halting compilation.

CMP_SCI-4200-Python-for-DS-Project-6-Aut.Title: YouTube Comment NLP Pipeline
CMP_SCI-4200-Python-for-DS-Project-6-Aut.Description: A Python pipeline that pulls public comments through the YouTube Data API with pagination, stores them as structured JSON, and cleans the text (URLs, emojis, mentions, hashtags, punctuation, stop words).
